s: A company is deploying a newbig data analytics cluster across multiple Availability Zones. All nodes must have read/write access to shared file storage that is highly available,POSIX-compatible, and high throughput.
o: Use AWS Storage Gateway (file gateway) backed by Amazon S3
Use Amazon EFS in General Purpose performance mode
Use Amazon EFS with Max I/O performance mode
e: Dis the right choice:EFS with Max I/O modeis designed formassively parallel workloads like big data. It supports high throughput and concurrent access from many EC2 nodes across AZs. A(Storage Gateway) is not optimized for high-performance, low-latency compute clusters. Bis limited in performance (latency optimized for single-threaded workloads). C(EBS) cannot be shared across AZs and is not POSIX-compatible for concurrent multi-node access. Reference:https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/performance.html

w.y: Same scenario as the big data cluster question: "shared", "POSIX", "highly available" and "high throughput" across AZs point to Amazon EFS, and exam keys pick Max I/O for many parallel nodes.

o.A: File Gateway is a hybrid cache for S3, not a highly available, high-throughput cluster file system.
o.B: Also EFS; General Purpose is AWS's current recommendation, but older exam keys favor Max I/O for large parallel clusters.
o.C: EBS Multi-Attach is limited to one AZ and needs a cluster-aware file system.
o.D: Correct per key: EFS Max I/O for highly parallel, high-throughput access.

st: Exam keys still pick Max I/O, but AWS now recommends General Purpose mode (with Elastic throughput) for nearly all workloads; Max I/O is a legacy choice with higher latency.
alt: B is defensible today: AWS recommends General Purpose mode with Elastic throughput, and throughput is set by the throughput mode rather than the performance mode.
